# Daily Life Hacks

> Practical nutrition tips, easy healthy recipes, and kitchen hacks for everyday life. Food-first, no supplements, no drama. Also home to original, publicly auditable grocery nutrition economics data: which foods deliver the most fiber and protein per dollar in the US.

## About

Daily Life Hacks is a food and nutrition site run by David Miller. The content focuses on simple, repeatable meals and science-backed nutrition advice for busy people. American audience, English only. The site also publishes original data studies on grocery nutrition economics, with every dataset released as a public CSV.

## Topics

- Nutrition: gut health, fiber, protein, healthy fats, reading food labels
- Recipes: quick weeknight dinners, meal prep, one-pot meals, air fryer recipes, sourdough
- Tips: kitchen organization, food storage, grocery shopping on a budget, cooking basics
- Data studies: fiber per dollar, protein per dollar, grocery price tracking

## Original Data Studies

These are original analyses, not aggregated from other publishers. Nutrition values come from USDA FoodData Central. Prices come from BLS Average Price data and dated Walmart national listings. All values use an as-purchased basis with USDA edible-fraction (refuse) adjustments. Every public CSV has an `fdc_id` column and a `source_url` column. `source_url` is the public FoodData Central food-details page for that id (`https://fdc.nal.usda.gov/food-details/{fdc_id}/nutrients`). A cell is left blank when no single FoodData Central record was determinable. Full methodology and limitations: https://www.daily-life-hacks.com/methodology/

- Fiber per Dollar study (53 foods ranked): https://www.daily-life-hacks.com/fiber-per-dollar-cheapest-high-fiber-foods/
- Protein per Dollar study (49 sources ranked): https://www.daily-life-hacks.com/protein-per-dollar-cheapest-protein-sources/
- Fiber per Dollar Calculator (interactive tool on the same dataset): https://www.daily-life-hacks.com/tools/fiber-per-dollar-calculator/
- All tools: https://www.daily-life-hacks.com/tools/

## Datasets (public CSV, free to reuse)

- Fiber per dollar raw data: https://www.daily-life-hacks.com/data/fiber-per-dollar-2026.csv
- Fiber per Dollar dataset page: https://www.daily-life-hacks.com/data/fiber-per-dollar-2026/
- Protein per dollar raw data: https://www.daily-life-hacks.com/data/protein-per-dollar-2026.csv
- Protein per Dollar dataset page: https://www.daily-life-hacks.com/data/protein-per-dollar-2026/
- Hugging Face mirror (fiber and protein flagships): https://huggingface.co/datasets/moshiko123/daily-life-hacks-grocery-nutrition-per-dollar

Each ranking CSV includes every food, nutrient value, package and price inputs, edible-fraction adjustment, price basis, and calculated per-dollar value used in the corresponding study, plus `fdc_id` and `source_url` when a single FoodData Central record was determinable.

Blank `fdc_id` cells are intentional. Unpopped popcorn kernels stay blank because the fiber study could not tie them to a published FoodData Central record, and the same blank follows that row into the fiber rankings. Textured vegetable protein stays blank because that row is a manufacturer label, not a FoodData Central record. Frozen shelled edamame stays blank on the fiber study and the produce fiber ranking because that fiber row is unresolved; the protein files do carry FDC 168410 for the same food. Complete-protein pair rows stay blank because each row is two foods. Fast-food menu items stay blank because their numbers come from chain nutrition pages. Restaurant lines in the day-cost menus (Starbucks, Wendy's, Taco Bell, and McDonald's) stay blank for the same reason.

## Data Verification

Published nutrition figures are checked against USDA FoodData Central, while prices use BLS Average Price data where available and dated retailer listings for other items. The public CSVs let readers inspect the calculations and price basis, subject to the source-detail limitations above. Prices are scheduled for a quarterly re-audit; relevant BLS staple prices are monitored monthly. Errors are corrected publicly with dated notes in the affected study. Correction policy and audit process: https://www.daily-life-hacks.com/methodology/

## Attribution and license

The original Daily Life Hacks selection, arrangement, calculations, field descriptions, and explanatory material are licensed under CC BY 4.0. Source facts and third-party material keep their own status and terms. When citing figures or reusing the datasets, attribute "Daily Life Hacks" and link to the specific study URL (preferred) or https://www.daily-life-hacks.com/data/. Mark any changes. Full scope and copy-ready attribution: https://www.daily-life-hacks.com/data-reuse/.

## Content Guidelines

All content follows a food-first approach. No supplement recommendations, no medical claims, no detox language. Recipes include accurate nutrition info, realistic quantities, and correct cooking times.
